findings: Portfolio decision for the model book: 100% stocks. The regime optimum is 150% stocks, 50% borrowed. Of the 6 active policies walked forward since 1940 (holding stocks is one of them; the learner that weights them is a seventh), the one with the strongest evidence of making a risk-averse investor better off than holding stocks is regime stocks (utility t -0.2, against 1.2 expected from the best of 9 useless strategies), so the gate moves 0% of the way toward it.

Regimes: 4 states of stocks, bonds and gold together. Next month is most likely calm bull (88%), where stocks and Treasuries have moved with a correlation of +0.14; in the stressed state (7%) it is +0.13.

Walked forward with costs since 1940: Sharpe 0.50 for the regime allocation, 0.64 gated, 0.65 for the learner over six policies, against 0.64 for holding stocks, 0.65 for 60/40 and 0.52 for risk parity; worst drawdowns, in the same order, -62%, -52%, -41%, -52%, -37% and -28%.
Deflated for the 9 strategies tried (the six policies, the gated engine, the learner and the stock-only decision engine), the chance the best one (regime stocks) has a real edge in Sharpe is 1%.

Simulated ten years from today's regime odds (5,000 paths of historical months drawn by state): all stocks end at a median 2.03x real (5% to 95%: 0.88x to 4.13x) with a 36% chance of a drawdown deeper than 30%; 60/40 at 1.72x (1.01x to 2.70x) with 9%.
Replayed through the Depression (1929-09 to 1932-06), today's mixes return, in real terms: all stocks -76%, 60/40 -49%, risk parity -14%, the regime optimum -90%.
